03 Because this is a race where no one dares to let go of the accelerator first.

03 The brakes are right at your feet, why can't you step on them first?

03 Because this is a race where no one dares to let go of the accelerator first.

03 The brakes are right at your feet, why can' While advocating for a slowdown, a bottom line was drawn that could not be stopped. This structure has appeared once before in history: the Cold War nuclear arms race. Both the US and the USSR knew they had enough nuclear weapons and knew the dangers, but neither side dared to unilaterally stop. What ultimately slowed the race down was not a change of heart, but "mutual visibility": treaties, verification, and transparency mechanisms. Dario's solution essentially brings "verification" into AI, proceeding in three steps: First, Anthropic unilaterally introduces "embedded evaluators"—giving third-party organizations like METR official work cards, workstations, and laptops, with permissions comparable to the internal risk control team, and contracts guaranteeing that their findings will not be reviewed by the company's editors; second, coordination among democratic countries; and third, global coordination, including with China. The "independent evaluator access" promised by Ultraman is an echo of the same idea—which translates to: Welcome to my house to inspect the goods. But criticism came just as quickly. Hours after publishing a lengthy article, Stability AI founder Emad Mostaque launched a scathing attack: "The power of evaluators will be negligible—don't forget, even the OpenAI board, which had formal authority, couldn't do anything back then." His logic is even sharper: if the real concern is competitors catching up through distillation, the only effective action is to stop training, not audit it. There's another reality we can't forget: when the rules of the game become "universal slowdown," the players at the forefront are actually the biggest beneficiaries—their moat can be reinforced with "safety." Anthropic, which has been the loudest in calling for the brakes, is rumored to have a $2 trillion valuation and a Nasdaq listing in October. When Dario was pressed in a CBS interview about whether it was possible to slow down while maintaining the lead, he gave a rare honest answer: "This is the toughest dilemma… honestly, I don't know if it's possible." So the question arises: are those who shout the loudest about braking always the ones in the lead? 04 Musk is building a 12-year chain of evidence. Looking at Musk's four consecutive statements, there's another, more sober interpretation. From recommending "Superintelligence" in 2014, to sounding the alarm in 2023, and now strongly supporting Dario—this isn't a spur-of-the-moment decision; it's a chain of evidence accumulated over 12 years. Every post silently says: See, I told you so. When AI really does cause a major incident someday, this record will be the strongest disclaimer. This is commercially unassailable—keeping warnings is instinctive for all intelligent people. Moreover, while issuing warnings to slow down, he himself didn't ease off the accelerator at all: According to public reports, in February of this year, xAI merged into SpaceX; in June, it acquired the parent company of AI programming company Cursor for approximately $60 billion; the Colossus supercomputer provided computing power to Grok day and night. He warned the industry to slow down, but he himself kept the accelerator running—this image encapsulates the full meaning of this article's title. However, we shouldn't dismiss everything as mere rhetoric. Coxon's departure warning, the fact that his code accounts for at least 70% of his work, and the real-world agent-assisted attacks—these aren't public relations rhetoric; they're data. Even those who create AI admit they can't keep up with what they've created—this signal itself carries more weight than any moral appeal. There's a recurring, proven pattern in business history: technology is tamed not by the self-discipline of its inventors, but by systems outside the inventors themselves. Seatbelts in cars, clinical trials for drugs, and internet privacy laws—none of these were achieved through industry self-regulation. AI will likely be no exception. The real question isn't who calls the brakes, but whether the "verification mechanism" can evolve from a verbal promise into a hard constraint like the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. The brakes and the accelerator are on the same foot. Which foot will release first—this question shouldn't ultimately be answered by the person pedaling.

data.title: Robinhood Chain has not yet released its distribution benefits.
data.description:
Written by: Saksham Diwan,CoinDesk Research

Translated by: Starbase Accelerator

Report Overview

In September 2026, CoinDesk Research released a research report on Robinhood Chain. The report points out that even before Robinhood's large retail user base has been fully integrated, its on-chain ecosystem has already formed a strong liquidity and revenue foundation. Over the past 30 days, Robinhood Chain TVL has increased by approximately 90% to $757 million, with the latest daily DEX trading volume reaching $1.69 billion, and cumulative holder revenue of approximately $20 million. Robinhood's own application users currently contribute only about 1%–2% of the on-chain transaction volume.

The core logic of the report is that Robinhood Chain's truly difficult-to-replicate advantage lies in its distribution capabilities. Robinhood boasts tens of millions of retail users, a mature consumer finance brand, and the ability to mint tokenized shares through authorized participants, but currently, the vast majority of its on-chain growth still comes from crypto-native users. If its retail users gradually migrate to the blockchain in the future, the existing TVL, DEX, Launchpad, tokenized shares, and stablecoin ecosystem may only be the starting point for growth. The report mainly focuses on the following dimensions: Activity and Liquidity Growth: TVL is growing rapidly, DEX trading volume has entered the top ranks of the industry, and considerable on-chain revenue is beginning to form. User and Traffic Structure: Current trading is mainly contributed by crypto-native scenarios such as Uniswap, trading terminals, and Launchpad; Robinhood application users still account for a very low percentage. Launchpad and Uniswap V4: New asset issuance has become an important source of trading volume; the programmable Hook mechanism has achieved large-scale application on the Robinhood Chain. Tokenized Stocks and Stock Memecoin: Robinhood relies on its authorized participant minting mechanism to gain a structural advantage in on-chain stocks and has derived new trading models. Stablecoins, Lending, and RWA Infrastructure: Stablecoin supply, credit, and RWA scale are expanding simultaneously, providing a settlement foundation for future Robinhood retail users to enter the on-chain ecosystem. On-chain activity is growing rapidly. Robinhood Chain currently boasts on-chain activity levels that are disproportionate to its development stage. In the past 30 days, its TVL has increased by approximately 90% to $757 million, reaching approximately $801 million on September 2nd, placing it near 12th among public chains in terms of TVL. More noteworthy than TVL is its capital turnover efficiency. Robinhood Chain's latest daily DEX trading volume has reached approximately $1.69 billion, accounting for about 17% of the global DEX trading volume. Its cumulative DEX trading volume over the past 7 days is approximately $8.2 billion, second only to Solana's $18.1 billion and Ethereum's $9.8 billion, and higher than BSC and Base. This means that Robinhood Chain is not relying on large amounts of capital to accumulate TVL, but rather has established a high frequency of on-chain transaction activity. Compared to its approximately $757 million TVL, its daily DEX trading volume is more than double the TVL, indicating a high level of on-chain capital turnover.

The Real Variable: Robinhood Users Haven't Entered the Market

Over 98% of Transactions Come from Crypto Native Users

The most significant characteristic of the Robinhood Chain is that the aforementioned growth almost entirely does not come from Robinhood's own users.

On-chain swaps within the Robinhood app are primarily routed through 0x, and even at peak times, these transactions only account for approximately 1%–2% of the Robinhood Chain's daily transaction volume.

The vast majority of remaining activity comes from third-party trading terminals, Uniswap, Launchpad, and other crypto-native trading platforms. Trading terminals are particularly notable, with weekly trading volume growing from less than $20 million at the end of June to over $1.2 billion recently. Robinhood Chain currently accounts for approximately 33% of the total cross-chain trading terminals. Therefore, Robinhood Chain's current TVL, trading volume, and revenue are closer to a "stress test without Robinhood user participation": before the parent company's most important distribution resources have been fully released, the crypto-native market has already established a liquidity cycle of considerable scale.

Uniswap Becomes the Core Liquidity Hub

These crypto-native traffic are highly concentrated on Uniswap. Currently, Uniswap contributes approximately 77% of the DEX trading volume on Robinhood Chain, Ramses approximately 6%, and UP approximately 5%.

This concentration has even had a reverse impact on Uniswap's own cross-chain structure—Robinhood Chain currently contributes over 50% of Uniswap's total chain transaction volume, becoming the first non-Ethereum network to reach this level.

Even more noteworthy is the application of Uniswap V4 Hook on Robinhood Chain.

After its launch in January 2025, V4 Hooks allowed developers to add programmable logic such as dynamic fees, limit orders, custom issuance mechanisms, and oracles to liquidity pools, but early adoption was slow. Robinhood Chain was one of the first ecosystems to transform Hooks from an "optional feature" into actual trading infrastructure. Launchpad and the stock Memecoin heavily utilize V4 Hooks for fee routing, liquidity bootstrapping, and asset issuance, making Robinhood Chain a significant source of cross-chain V4 Hook pool transactions in a short period.

Launchpad Becomes a Driver of Transaction Volume

Daily Launchpad Transaction Volume Exceeds $600 Million

Robinhood Chain's other core growth driver is Launchpad. On September 1st, its Launchpad daily transaction volume exceeded $600 million, with Pons accounting for approximately 60% and long.xyz accounting for approximately 25%.

From a full-chain comparison, Robinhood Chain currently contributes approximately 14% of Launchpad revenue, ranking third, behind only Solana and BSC.

These asset issuance activities simultaneously drive trading demand to DEXs like Uniswap. Therefore, Launchpad is not an independent segment, but rather a significant source of Robinhood Chain's high DEX trading volume and on-chain revenue. This creates a relatively clear growth path for Robinhood Chain: new asset issuance attracts speculative and trading demand, trading activity flows into DEXs and generates fees, and liquidity and revenue further attract new protocols and market-making capital. Robinhood Chain's Launchpad growth is highly correlated with Uniswap V4's programmable liquidity mechanism. Traditional Launchpad addresses "how assets are issued," while V4 Hook further allows projects to customize post-issuance fees, liquidity, and trading rules. This means that Launchpad, AMM, and liquidity management are being compressed from three relatively independent components into a single infrastructure. Robinhood Chain's current rapid growth in trading volume is essentially partly due to this high degree of coupling between new asset issuance and secondary liquidity. Tokenized equity constitutes a structural advantage. Robinhood accounts for approximately 53% of on-chain equity. Compared to Launchpad and Memecoin, tokenized equity may be a more difficult advantage for Robinhood Chain to replicate by other public chains. Currently, Robinhood accounts for approximately 53% of the total on-chain tokenized equity from various issuers. Its key advantage comes from its authorized participant minting mechanism: Robinhood can build a supply of tokenized assets around real stocks, rather than simply relying on third parties to cross-chain or repackage assets. This means that the Robinhood Chain is not only a trading venue for tokenized stocks, but also controls the entry point for some assets onto the chain. Compared to public chains that rely solely on liquidity incentives to attract RWA assets, this issuance and distribution capability constitutes a stronger structural barrier. Stock Memecoin Forms a New Trading Structure The recent growth of tokenized stocks has also spawned a special "stock Memecoin" model. Some Memecoins on long.xyz do not directly form AMM pools with stablecoins, but are paired with corresponding tokenized stocks. Therefore, the price of Memecoin is actually a relative price of "stock tokens / Memecoin". When a user buys Memecoin, the corresponding stock token enters the liquidity pool, thus directly linking Launchpad speculation with tokenized stock liquidity. Currently, some stock Memecoins already account for 20%–40% of the corresponding stock's on-chain circulating supply. For example, BONER accounts for approximately 42% of the on-chain HIMS circulating supply, MOO approximately 27% of MU, and AI approximately 18% of NVDA. However, this high percentage reflects the still small size of the tokenized stock market. Taking AI/NVDA as an example, even at its peak, its size was only equivalent to about 0.0048% of NVIDIA's market capitalization. Therefore, currently, stock Memecoins have almost no impact on traditional stock prices themselves, but they already have a significant influence on the still small on-chain stock market. Meanwhile, since Robinhood stock tokens can only be minted through authorized participants, during periods when US stock markets are closed and minting and redemption are restricted, if Memecoin trading accounts for an excessively high on-chain circulation, it may cause the tokenized stock price to temporarily deviate from the traditional market reference price. Stablecoins and RWA are forming the underlying settlement foundation. Stablecoin supply is approaching $900 million. Beyond trading activities, the settlement foundation of the Robinhood Chain is also expanding simultaneously. Currently, the on-chain stablecoin supply is approximately $868 million, an increase of approximately $118 million in the past 7 days, representing a growth of 15.8%, of which USDG accounts for approximately 63%. At the same time, on-chain lending TVL continues to grow, and the active RWA market capitalization has reached approximately $197 million. The importance of these data lies in the fact that they represent Robinhood Chain's expansion from a simple high-frequency trading network into a financial infrastructure capable of payments, collateralization, lending, and real-world asset trading. Stablecoins handle settlement, lending protocols provide credit, tokenized stocks and RWA provide the asset side, and DEX and Launchpad provide liquidity and trading support. If Robinhood migrates more retail users to the chain in the future, this infrastructure is already capable of handling the corresponding assets and trading activities without needing to build it from scratch. In summary, what's most noteworthy about Robinhood Chain right now isn't just the 90% increase in TVL or the $1.69 billion daily DEX trading volume, but rather the premise behind these figures: Robinhood's true distribution advantage has yet to be fully realized. Currently, approximately 98%–99% of on-chain transactions originate from crypto-native users, with Robinhood's own app users contributing only about 1%–2%. However, Robinhood Chain has already established a TVL of $757 million, weekly transaction volume in the billions of dollars, accumulated holder income of approximately $20 million, and a preliminary financial ecosystem comprised of Uniswap, Launchpad, tokenized stocks, stablecoins, lending, and RWA. This differentiates Robinhood Chain's growth logic from that of typical new public chains. Most new chains need to attract liquidity through incentives before seeking real users; Robinhood, on the other hand, already possesses tens of millions of retail users and mature financial distribution channels, although these users have not yet entered the chain on a large scale. Simultaneously, its ability to authorize participants to mint tokenized stocks gives Robinhood an asset entry point in RWA, especially in the area of ​​stock tokenization, that is difficult for other public chains to replicate. Therefore, the real variable the report focuses on is not how much growth Robinhood Chain can currently achieve through native crypto transactions, but rather when and at what conversion rate Robinhood can bring its Web2 finance users onto the chain. If this distribution funnel gradually opens, then the current TVL, transaction volume, and revenue are more likely to become the baseline for future growth; conversely, if Robinhood fails to complete user migration, then the sustainability of its current growth structure, which heavily relies on Launchpad, Memecoin, and native crypto transactions, still needs further verification. The core investment logic of Robinhood Chain is essentially a judgment on whether "distribution capabilities can be transformed into on-chain financial activities."

data.title: AI is starting to surpass mathematicians: They're really scared.
data.description:
Over the past week, artificial intelligence has made continuous breakthroughs in the field of mathematics: from the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem that has plagued the mathematical community for 90 years to the formal proof of Fermat's Last Theorem, machines are increasingly involved in mathematical research.

Wired contributor Isabella Ward interviewed Cornell University mathematician Steven Strogatz to try to understand what this change means for mathematicians.

Wired contributor Isabella Ward interviewed Cornell University mathematician Steven Strogatz to try to understand what this change means for mathematicians.

Screenshot of a Wired report

Mathematics is entering an unfamiliar era

When Steven Strogatz spoke about the breakthroughs that artificial intelligence has brought to the field of mathematics in the past week, the mathematician couldn't help but shed tears. “This science is exciting,” he said, “but it comes with a lot of unpleasant human factors.” On September 8th, OpenAI announced that it had solved a 90-year-old mathematical problem using tens of thousands of agents. The problem has a $1 million prize, and OpenAI's solution still needs independent verification. This achievement is based on a strategy proposed by Spanish mathematicians Diego Córdoba and Luis Martínez-Zoroa. However, immediately after OpenAI announced its results, mathematician Tristan Buckmaster raised questions. Buckmaster stated that OpenAI rushed into the solution after learning of his work with Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge. He also claimed that OpenAI attempted to influence who should ultimately receive credit for the work. According to Strogatz, this controversy is merely a symptom of the dramatic changes taking place in the field of mathematics. Artificial intelligence is significantly accelerating mathematical research, and corporate labs are vying for headlines. Strogatz believes this competition is even related to the logic of vying for market attention before a major IPO. Strogaz and mathematician Alex Townsend have co-authored a new book, *Big Math*, discussing how mathematics is increasingly surpassing human comprehension. The book will be published in November. Just a week ago, Anthropic announced that Claude had proven 29,500 small theorems and completed the formalization of the existing proof of the famous Fermat's Last Theorem. Other mathematicians had been working on this project for years. In August, OpenAI also announced progress on 10 other long-standing mathematical problems. Strogatz believes that AI is making mathematical breakthroughs happen faster. But what this means for those who have dedicated their lives to mathematical research is far less clear. "I think 2026 will be remembered as either a 'miracle year' or a 'horror year' for mathematics because so much is happening," he says. He adds that if you want to make groundbreaking mathematical achievements in the future, "without AI, you won't be able to compete." AI Solves Problems, But Humans Aren't Necessarily Happier. Strogatz's collaborator, Townsend, is already using AI to accelerate his research. Recently, he used ChatGPT to help solve a numerical linear algebra problem that had plagued the mathematical community for decades. Near the end of the interview, Townsend went into Strogatz's attic. He and his collaborator had previously stated that without this technology, the amount of work they would have had to do, and the ratio of input to return, would have been unbearably high. AI has indeed helped Townsend's research, but it has also changed his perspective on mathematics and his place in the field. "I'm actually a little sad. I've dedicated 15 years of my life to mathematical research, and right at the peak of my career, when I was most productive and mathematically capable, that peak ability is no longer there." Because something has surpassed him. In the past, becoming a world-class mathematician, making outstanding research, and pushing the boundaries of knowledge was itself a tremendous source of excitement. "But now, I feel like I'm no longer at the forefront of knowledge. I'm the one leading an AI agent, and that feels completely different." "I feel utterly threatened." For Strogatz, mathematics right now is like a horror movie: AI, driven by systems that humans don't yet fully understand, is closing in little by little. "But the movie isn't over yet." "Instinctively, I was really terrified." [Image of Cornell University mathematician Steven Strogatz. Source: Strogatz, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons] What does this 90-year-old mathematical problem really mean? Regarding the significance of OpenAI's solution to the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, Strogatz doesn't believe it has much practical application. It's a highly theoretical mathematical problem, of little interest to engineers working in civil engineering or aerodynamics. It's a "very, very obscure problem." In his view, it's more like a marketing tool to showcase machine capabilities. Only a very small number of pure mathematicians are truly interested in the Navier-Stokes singularity problem. It doesn't directly affect others. "But for OpenAI, proving itself stronger than Anthropic might be worth a trillion dollars." And who should ultimately receive the $1 million prize? Strogats hopes that Cordova and Martinez-Zorroa will get the money, but he believes things can't be judged so simply. Two other people should also be seriously discussed: Tristan Buckmaster of New York University, and the young mathematician Levent Alperger. One could even argue that Buckmaster should receive the prize. This is because just days before OpenAI announced its findings, Buckmaster and Alperger had already published solutions to three problems highly relevant to the Navier-Stokes problem. These problems are somewhat easier, but they are still serious and important mathematical problems in themselves. “They’ve already gone down this path. I think they could have gotten there, but we didn’t know.” Strogats didn’t know Bachmaster, but from what he’d seen, Bachmaster was very meticulous about attribution and credit. “He was very gentlemanly about it. I have great respect for the way he handled it.” But Strogats also felt sorry for Bachmaster—he might ultimately not get what he’d been pursuing his entire career. What else can human mathematicians do? Even if AI can solve more and more mathematical problems, human mathematicians still have an important task: understanding what the machines are actually doing. Strogatz calls this ability "proof digestion." That is, interpreting the proofs generated by machines into a form that humans can understand and appreciate. Currently, the best "digestion" work still comes from human experts. So, will this become the last line of defense for human mathematicians? Will humans become great interpreters of machine work? Strogatz believes that for some time to come, humans may still possess this special ability—translating machine results into languages ​​that humans can understand. However, he also predicts that this ability will eventually be surpassed by machines. On the other hand, applied mathematics may not be so easily replaced by AI. The reason is that it deals with the real world, and the real world itself is full of chaos. "The more chaotic a field is, the harder it is for AI to handle." Therefore, disciplines such as economics, international relations, and sociology may be relatively safe for a period of time. Mathematics itself has an infinite number of problems, but only a portion of them are interesting to humans. So, a more fundamental question arises: Who judges what constitutes good mathematical taste? Will machines possess an aesthetic sensibility that resonates with humans? There is currently no indication that they already possess this ability. But Strogatz also sees no reason why machines cannot, through training, eventually become highly adept at aesthetics. Mathematics is being "destroyed" and also "revolutionized." Strogatz argues that, from different perspectives, pure mathematics is facing two completely different fates. It can be described as both "destroyed" and "revolutionized." Many problems cherished by mathematicians are being solved. However, many mathematicians are not happy about this. Because they enjoy these questions and the challenges of thinking about them. If someone only cares about the answer and not the process of finding it, then of course they'll be satisfied with AI. But from another perspective, AI also democratizes mathematics. Now, everyone can participate in mathematics. Strogatz was unwilling to stand in his ivory tower and say: "I'm 67 years old. I've spent my whole life training myself to have the ability to do these things. I don't want you to come here without contributing anything." This attitude is unreasonable. When machines always reach the summit first, what may truly disappear is the motivation of some mathematicians to engage in mathematical research. In the past, there were always those who aspired to be the first to reach the summit of mathematics. But if machines always reach the top first, humanity may no longer be able to make climbing the highest peak its goal. "We always lose." If a person's motivation comes precisely from being the first to reach the summit, then the game may already be over. Of course, one could also ask in return: Why must this be the only game? Strogatz gave two examples. He wouldn't participate in Wimbledon, but he would still play tennis. Humans aren't as strong as computer chess programs, yet they still enjoy playing chess. So, could the future of mathematics be similar? Mathematics might become a beautiful game that we're not good at, but still enjoy. This future isn't impossible. However, it will bring a series of real-world problems. If mathematics ultimately becomes just a game that humans enjoy playing, then why would anyone pay mathematicians to do mathematics? If all the work is done by AI, there will be no need to invest in having human mathematicians do the same work. “Unless we stop this trend, it seems like a very likely trajectory.” Will mathematics become a “coal mine canary”? Strogatz believes that mathematics may be the first “battleground” for humanity in the face of this change. "I feel that we are the first human battlefield standing here: we are on the verge of losing our human comprehension." Fortunately, the practical implications for mathematics may not be so high yet. But mathematicians will be the first to feel what it truly means when machines begin to surpass humans' core capabilities in a highly intellectual field. "We'll see what this feels like for humans." "Are we becoming the canary in the coal mine, giving a preview of what humanity will face in the future?" Reference: Isabella Ward. ‘I’m Really Terrified’: A Mathematician Grapples With AI’s Recent Breakthroughs. WIRED, Sep 12, 2026 6:00 AM. https://www.wired.com/story/mathematician-steven-strogatz-grapples-with-ai-recent-breakthroughs/

data.title: Goldman Sachs reverses course, overturning consensus on interest rate hikes overnight.
data.description:
Monday opened with a rude awakening. Bitcoin briefly dipped below $77,000, retracing to the $76,000 level, weighing heavily on the market due to Wednesday's interest rate meeting. Currently, the market has priced in an interest rate hike at 85%, even approaching 90%. However, on Friday evening in New York, a seemingly small event occurred on Wall Street. Something as seemingly insignificant as a few figures in a research report brought this consensus reversal to a close. Goldman Sachs withdrew its forecast after the market closed last Friday, changing its stance from holding rates steady to raising rates by 25 basis points. It was the last major bank on Wall Street to change its forecast. By this point, all the major investment banks had turned their backs on this issue [1]. A little over a week ago, not raising rates was the baseline scenario for many major banks. With the release of the August non-farm payrolls and the August CPI, the balance was completely reversed in just a few days. Goldman Sachs' Reasons

Goldman Sachs' Reasons

The research report is straightforward. The August CPI only slightly raised Goldman Sachs' forecast for the August core PCE to 0.26%, but did not change its fundamental judgment on inflation. The inflation data is just a backdrop. What really prompted Goldman Sachs to change its tune is the market's positioning: the market has already priced in a nearly 90% probability of an interest rate hike. If the Fed does not take action, it is likely to provoke a violent market reaction, and the FOMC (Federal Reserve Interest Rate Meeting) does not want to see such a reaction[1]. Two years ago, in September 2024, the Federal Reserve initiated a rate-cutting cycle, cutting interest rates by 50 basis points on its first move, more than double the market expectation of 25 basis points. At that time, the core CPI in the United States was still above 3%[1]. Two years later, in this September, the core CPI has fallen to 2.4%, a five-year low, but the Federal Reserve is preparing to raise interest rates[1][2]. In the same month, the same institution. Rate cuts when inflation is above 3%, and rate hikes when inflation is 2.4%. In just two years, the Federal Reserve's judgment criteria seem to have changed entirely. Kevin Warsh criticized the so-called "Hall of Mirrors problem" in his first speech at Jackson Hole. He criticized the interdependence between the Fed and the market: the market prices based on the Fed's guidance, and the Fed judges the situation based on market prices—both sides think they are looking at reality, but in reality, they are seeing the other (this reminds me of Soros's reflexivity). He also promised to end forward guidance and stop feeding the market expectations in advance. James Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus, called Goldman Sachs's change of heart Wall Street's "Wall of Mirrors." His words were direct: the inflation outlook has not changed substantially, and raising interest rates is just to appease Wall Street. Raising interest rates will not produce oil, expand refining capacity, or repair the cut-off shipping lanes. What raising interest rates can do is suppress demand, investment, employment, and household purchasing power[1]. Using the mirror wall as an analogy, it is ironic that Wall Street is not seeing the economic reality, but its own positions and expectations. It thinks it is responding to the macroeconomy, but it is actually just responding to itself (what comes to mind is Pavlov's dog - conditioned reflex, not thinking). He put out a few numbers. Wage growth has fallen to 3.1%. There is no spiral of wages and prices pushing each other up, no verifiable double inflation, and no evidence that the energy shock is embedded in long-term prices[1]. He concluded by saying that if the Federal Reserve under Warsh was merely raising interest rates to endorse the narrative of the futures market, then Warsh's critique of the Hall of Mirrors and his promise to end forward guidance were meaningless[1]. Sun Tzu's Art of War states that a skillful strategist moves the enemy without being moved by them. In this instance, the one being moved is the Federal Reserve. Opposing voices are equally compelling. KPMG Chief Economist Diane Swonk pointed out that the increase in core CPI in August was concentrated in the service sector, with super core services rising 0.5% month-on-month and 3% year-on-year, which is quite hot. According to her calculations, the overall PCE rose 0.4% in August, and the core rose 0.3%, with the adjusted core PCE growth rate at 3.4%, which is much further from the 2% target for core CPI. Her conclusion is that there will be three more interest rate hikes by early 2027, and the probability of unanimous approval in this vote has increased [1]. Two questions point to two questions. One question is whether the Federal Reserve should raise interest rates with a core CPI of 2.4%. Another question is whether the Fed dares not to raise rates when the market has already priced in a 90% chance of a rate hike. The first question concerns inflation, the second concerns authority. Goldman Sachs' research report answers the latter question. Once a central bank begins to serve market expectations, it loses control. Giving the market what it wants may seem like following the trend, but in reality, it's being led by the nose. When the market turns around as expected, it will turn around again, and after several such reversals, its resolve will crumble. The *Tao Te Ching* says, "Not knowing the constant, acting rashly brings misfortune." For those holding diamond positions, all these debates ultimately boil down to the same thing: price. Bitcoin retreated from $80,000 to $77,000, wiping out the floating shares bought at the high. Even if the interest rate hike actually happens, it's just another step back. What really matters isn't Wednesday's interest rate decision. A mirror doesn't reflect the truth; it only reflects the image of the person standing before it.

data.title: Explanation of slang related to currency crimes: material properties, washing materials, adulteration
data.description:
Organized crime networks in East and Southeast Asia employ a large amount of coded language with distinct regional characteristics, cultural attributes, and industry verticals, posing a significant comprehension barrier for investigators and researchers—especially those unfamiliar with Chinese language and culture.

Bitrace plans to continuously disclose and analyze this industry jargon to help relevant personnel better conduct their work. This article is the second in the series, introducing the specialized term "料" (liao) in the Chinese-language field of online cryptocurrency money laundering.

Liao Laundering

Liao (料) has different meanings in various black and gray industry verticals. In the field of cryptocurrency money laundering, it specifically refers to fiat currency related to illegal activities such as fraud, extortion, online gambling, and human trafficking. In most cases, it is the electronic balance of bank accounts or other financial platform accounts to be laundered.

Currently, there are various forms of liaison laundering, including Card-to-USDT, QR-to-USDT, Cash-to-USDT, and Cash-to-Material Assets (usually precious metals or other marketable commodities).

Despite the different forms, the underlying logic remains the same—converting traceable electronic fiat currency into untraceable cryptocurrencies, goods, or cash to evade law enforcement crackdowns or financial platform scrutiny. This article will only use the most common example, credit card rebates, for illustration. In a typical money laundering model for romance scams, a first-hand card-to-USDT (Guarantee Public Group Merchant) first deposits funds on a guarantee platform, then receives fiat currency funds directly from the victim using a bank card. Next, they purchase USDT at a higher price from a cooperating second-hand card-to-USDT (Guarantee Public Group Merchant), and finally transfer a portion of the purchased USDT to the fraudsters. In the case study, the first-hand money launderer and the second-hand money launderer jointly completed the money laundering and profited. However, actual money laundering activities are far more complex than the case study, involving deeper layers and more sophisticated currency exchange methods. In general, the lower the level and the closer to the victim, the higher the probability of funds being frozen by the judiciary, the easier it is for first-hand money launderers to be apprehended, and the higher the commission income that money laundering merchants can earn. In other words, first-hand money laundering is more dangerous than second-hand money laundering. Type of Money Laundering (Liao) In the previous chapter, we learned that money laundering materials can be classified according to different stages of laundering and that money laundering services at corresponding stages can be marketed. This chapter will introduce more methods for classifying money laundering materials. Classified by Victim Type

Classified by Victim Type

Primary School Student Scam (Pupil Liao): Refers to funds defrauded from primary school students. Fraudsters typically approach victims under the guise of online game top-ups or idol support, then threaten them with secretly transferring their parents' money, threatening to cause their parents to lose their jobs or face legal investigation if they don't.

Part-Time Job Scam (Part-time Job Liao): Refers to money defrauded by creating fake communities or apps, then enticing victims to transfer money to specific accounts or purchase designated fake goods under the pretense of part-time work.

Part-time Job Scam (Part-time Job Liao): Refers to money defrauded by creating fake communities or apps, then enticing victims to transfer money to specific accounts or purchase designated fake goods under the guise of part-time work.

... The main victims of this type of fraud are stay-at-home mothers and college students; "Se Liao" (or "Porn Liao") refers to the illegal gains obtained by inducing victims to participate in investment schemes or complete tasks through prostitution, watching pornography, etc., and finally deceiving them into paying money; "Pig Butchering Scam Liao" involves creating a fake persona to engage in online romance with a target, then inducing the victim to participate in fake investment projects, and finally illegally obtaining a large sum of money. When the victim is Chinese, this method is called "Pig Butchering Scam," and when the victim is Western, this method is called "Sheep Butchering Scam." Classified by Crime Type: Online Gambling Information (Online Gambling Liao): Refers to the fiat currency funds deposited by gamblers into online gambling platforms. These funds require simple laundering before circulation; this laundering process is commonly known as "Running Points." Ponzi Scheme Information (Ponzi Scheme Liao): Refers to funds paid by participants in Ponzi schemes to their superiors. Because Ponzi schemes operate for several months, money launderers have ample time to carry out their work. Chinese Authority Impersonation Information (Chinese Authority Impersonation Liao): Refers to funds illegally obtained by impersonating Chinese public security, procuratorial, and judicial officials to defraud ordinary citizens. Because so many Chinese students have been defrauded by this method, the FBI specifically created this translation in its report. The preceding text briefly introduced several common types of adulteration (or "adulteration"). Due to differences in the type of illegal activity, its lifecycle, and the type of victim, the timing and intensity of judicial intervention will vary. From the perspective of money launderers, this means that different adulterations have different levels of toxicity and should be subject to different commission rates. For example, few gamblers actively report themselves to online gambling platforms; gambling-related adulterations are relatively low-risk and should be subject to the lowest commission rates. Similarly, in the months leading up to the collapse of a Ponzi scheme, victims will not proactively report the crime until the last person is completely unable to recover their funds. Low-risk methods are used initially, with high-risk methods applied in the final stage. In fraudulent cases impersonating law enforcement, victims almost always contact law enforcement quickly, making it the easiest time for funds to be frozen by the judiciary, and resulting in the highest laundering costs. Therefore, a fairly common deceptive practice in the money laundering field is "adulteration," where the "data owner" claims to need the money laundering group to process low-risk data, but actually delivers other high-risk data. The purpose is to save on laundering costs, at the cost of the money laundering group underestimating the toxicity of the data, leading to bank cards and cryptocurrency wallets being flagged for risk control.
